dialog.body: Public Works, this is Denise. How can I help you?
Good afternoon, Denise. Hello, hello. I hope you are having a good day and that you are well. My name is Declan Cullen. Can you hear me okay? I am on the speaker, my hands are not so free.
I can hear you fine, Mr. Cullen. Go ahead.

Thank you, thank you very much. You are kind. So, I am the landlord of a house, and I am calling about the street. I have been a landlord there many years, and I try never to bother the city. But I must tell you, I am not happy. It is the same every time it rains.
Okay. What's going on with the street? Where is it?
It is seventy-two Harrison Avenue. On the Fort Adams side, you know, going down toward the fort.
Seventy-two Harrison, got it. And what are you seeing there?

After the storm, the one last weekend, the snow and then the rain, Sunday into Monday, the water came and it did not go. Two days now, it is Wednesday, and still there is water. In front of the house the street is a pond. A real pond. And the cars, they drive through and they throw waves, like a boat. Wakes, yes? Onto the sidewalk, onto my tenants' steps.
Oof. How deep is it, would you say?

Up to the hubcaps. I measured with my eyes, from the window, the cars, the water is at the hubcaps. Monday it was more. Today a little less, but still. And every time, the same. The drain by the curb, I think it is full of leaves and the ice and the dirt. Nothing is going in.
Right, that sounds like the catch basin is clogged. Is it right in front of seventy-two or a little up the road?
Right in front, almost. Maybe two steps toward the corner. The grate, I can see only a little of it. The rest is under water and slush.
Okay.

So I am asking, with respect, please, can someone come and clean the drain? I have been waiting, and my tenants, they ask me, Mr. Cullen, why is the street like this, and I have no answer for them. It keeps happening. Each storm, the same.
I hear you. I'll put in a request for the crew to clean that basin. I can't tell you exactly what day they'll get there, they've got a lot of calls after this one.
Ah. I see. So you cannot do it. You are saying no. I understand, I understand, it is okay, you are very busy, everybody is busy. I thank you anyway.
No, no, I didn't say no. I said I'll put the request in. I just can't give you the day they'll come.
Excuse me? Sorry, the speaker, it is not so clear. You said you will put it in?
Yes. I'm entering the work order now. Seventy-two Harrison Avenue, clogged storm drain, standing water in the road. That's a yes.
Ah, I am sorry, Denise. I heard, you cannot say the day, and I thought, it is a refusal. Please forgive me. My ears, and this phone. Thank you. Thank you.
No worries at all. Easy to mix up. Can I ask, is the water coming into anyone's property, or is it just the street and the sidewalk?
For now, only the street and the sidewalk. The steps get wet from the cars. But my tenants, the downstairs one, she worries. If it comes higher, you know.
Okay, I'll note that so they know it's backing up near the houses. If it starts coming toward a door or a foundation, call us right back, and if it's an emergency, call 911.
Yes, yes, I will do that. But I must say, Denise, this is not the first time. Every winter, every big rain, I call, or I think to call. The street holds the water like a bowl.
Yeah, some of those low spots are bad. I'll add in the notes that it's a recurring problem there, so the crew sees it.
That is very good. Please. Because cleaning one time, and then three weeks later, again the same, it is not a solution. I am only a landlord, I am not an engineer, but I know a drain should drain.
[pause] You're right about that. I've got it written up. Do you want me to have someone call you when it's done, or when they've looked at it?
Yes, please, that would be wonderful. The number is four-zero-one, five-five-five, zero-one-seven-two.
Four-oh-one, five-five-five, oh-one-seven-two. That's what I have.
Exactly right. You are very careful, thank you.
And it's Cullen, C-U-L-L-E-N?
Yes, two L, two E, no, sorry, C-U-L-L-E-N. Two L, one E, one N. Forgive me.
Got it. Cullen. Okay, Mr. Cullen, the request is in. A crew will go out, clean the basin, and check that it's flowing. That water might take a bit to drop even after, since the road's been sitting.
Of course, of course. I only hope it will be soon. If it freezes tonight, then we have ice on top of the pond, and somebody will slip. It is dangerous for the elderly.
That's a fair point. I'll mention the freezing concern too. If it does ice up badly, call us again and we can flag it for sanding.
Thank you, I will. You have been very patient with an old man and his bad telephone.
Not a problem. Anything else I can do for you today?
No, that is everything. God bless you, Denise, and have a good afternoon, a peaceful day to you and your family.
You too, Mr. Cullen. Take care now.
Goodbye, goodbye. Thank you again.
